value.answer: Short term, it's generally considered safe for most adults, according to the NIH. Long-term safety is the open question. A preliminary American Heart Association abstract from November 2025 linked a year or more of use in people with chronic insomnia to higher rates of heart failure. It isn't peer-reviewed, it can't prove melatonin caused anything, and some experts think poor sleep may explain it. Melatonin does have side effects and can interact with other medicines, so check with a doctor or pharmacist before starting, especially if you take anything else or want to use it for longer than a short stretch.
